**Issue #1795 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #1795: Patch: a held backrow zone says it waits for an animated card's return, not a Reborn unit, when that is why
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Some backrow cards step out to fight as a unit for a turn and then go back. While one is away, the game keeps its backrow spot empty and nothing can be played there. The board marks the held spot, but its tooltip always says "Held for a Reborn unit". That's wrong in this case, and it leaves a player wondering why they can't use an empty space. Once built, the tooltip names the card the spot is being kept for.

## Why
- `apps/web/src/game/Zone.tsx:103`: the held-zone icon's `title` is always `t("Held for a Reborn unit")`.
- The view's held-zone flags cover both cases. `SideView.reserved`'s doc says: "B3.1 rule 6: the backrow zone an animated 'Animated on your turn' card will return to is held the same way."
- The engine's `is_reserved` checks an animated card's home (`state.homes`) as well as Reborn (`crates/engine/src/zones.rs:484-498`).
- A Reborn hold lasts only until the unit comes back, inside the same action. An animated card's home stays held until the end of its controller's turn, so the animated case is the one players mostly see.
- The view already says where an animated unit goes home: `UnitView.animated.home`. The card face already words it (`apps/web/src/cards/cardState.ts:93-98`, "back to its backrow (lane N)").
- No test covers the held-zone icon.

## Proposal
In `Zone`, for a held backrow zone, look for a unit on the same side whose `animated.home` is this lane. If there is one, title the icon "Held for {name} to return", using the unit's shown name. Otherwise keep the Reborn wording. Add the string to `zh-CN.json`. The unit is on the field, so its name is public and nothing hidden is shown (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Where it lands
- `apps/web/src/game/Zone.tsx`, `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json`, and a `Zone` test
- B3.1 rule 6 and R64, as the view's doc states them. No spec change.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] For a held backrow zone with a unit whose `animated.home` is its lane, the icon's title names that unit's return, not Reborn.
- [ ] A held zone with no such unit keeps "Held for a Reborn unit".
- [ ] `i18n.test.ts`, typecheck and eslint pass.

## Size and risks
Extra small: one component, one string and one test. There is no risk to play.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-4` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40116005722)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

When a held backrow zone is being kept for an animated "Animated on your turn" card, its icon's tooltip names that card: "Held for {name} to return". The card is a unit on the same side whose `UnitView.animated.home` is this lane, and the name is the one its card face shows. Any other held zone keeps "Held for a Reborn unit". The new string gets a `zh-CN.json` entry, a new `Zone` unit test covers both wordings, and `i18n.test.ts`, typecheck and eslint pass.

## Files to touch

| Path | Kind | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/game/Zone.tsx` | change | new module function `heldFor`; `Zone` reads `CatalogContext` and uses `heldFor` for the held icon's `title` |
| `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json` | change | one entry, `"Held for {name} to return"` |
| `apps/web/src/game/Zone.test.tsx` | new | the held icon's title, both wordings, both seats |

Do not touch: anything in `crates/` (no engine, view or wire change), `spec/`, `apps/web/src/wire/`, any other web component, CSS, `e2e/`, any `package.json` or config. This is governed by B3.1 rule 6 and R383 (`spec/rulings/R0383.md`: an animated "on your turn" card's backrow zone is held for its return) and R64 (`spec/rulings/R0064.md`: the Reborn hold). There is no new ruling and no spec change.

What the code does, checked:
- `UnitView.animated.home` is the engine's 1-based backrow lane, the same numbering as `Zone`'s `lane` prop. The R383 test in `apps/web/src/cards/cardState.test.tsx` pairs `home: 2` with `reserved.backrow[1]`.
- Homes are only ever backrow zones (`crates/engine/src/zones.rs`, `reserve_home`). Reborn holds are unit zones (`state_check.rs:793`).

## Steps

1. **`apps/web/src/game/Zone.tsx`, the imports.**
   - Change `import type { ReactElement } from "react";` to `import { useContext, type ReactElement } from "react";`.
   - Change `import type { PlayerView, Row } from "@jackioh/shared";` so it stays as it is. No new shared type is needed.
   - In the block of local imports, after the `import Card, { … } from "./Card.tsx";` line, add `import { CatalogContext, type CardLookup } from "./catalog.ts";`.
   - After the `./contract.ts` import, add `import { listedFace } from "./faces.ts";`.
   - `Side` and `sideView` are already imported from `./contract.ts`.

2. **`Zone.tsx`, the new function.** Add it after `zoneLabel` and before `export default function Zone`, exactly:

   ```tsx
   /**
    * What a held zone's icon says it waits for. B3.1 rule 6, R383: a backrow zone is held for the
    * animated "Animated on your turn" card on its side that goes back to it (`UnitView.animated.home`),
    * named as its face names it; any other hold is R64's, for a Reborn unit. The card stands on the
    * field, so its name is public (CLAUDE.md rule 7).
    */
   function heldFor(lookup: CardLookup | null, view: PlayerView, side: Side, row: Row, lane: number): string {
     const returning = row === "backrow" ? (sideView(view, side).units.find((unit) => unit?.animated?.home === lane) ?? null) : null;
     const face = returning === null ? null : listedFace(lookup, view, returning);
     return face === null ? t("Held for a Reborn unit") : t("Held for {name} to return", { name: face.name });
   }
   ```

   Both `t(...)` calls must keep a literal first argument, because `i18n.test.ts` reads those literals.

3. **`Zone.tsx`, inside `Zone`.**
   - Make `const lookup = useContext(CatalogContext);` the first line of the body, before `const { view, side, row, lane } = props;`. It must be called unconditionally, by the rules of hooks.
   - On line 103, replace `title={t("Held for a Reborn unit")}` with `title={heldFor(lookup, view, side, row, lane)}`.
   - Leave everything else on that line alone (the `reserved && !locked` guard, `className`, `aria-label={t("Reserved zone")}`). Because the call sits inside the `&&` branch, it runs only for a held zone.

4. **`apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json`.** Right after the line `"Held for a Reborn unit": "为复生单位保留",`, add:
   `  "Held for {name} to return": "为{name}返回保留",`
   Keep the file's two-space indentation and its trailing commas.

5. **`apps/web/src/game/Zone.test.tsx` (new).** Write it as described under Tests, copying the setup of `apps/web/src/game/flying-backrow.test.tsx`: `afterEach(cleanup)`, `const lookup = lookupFromDefs(CATALOG);` and a `CatalogContext.Provider` wrapper.

## Tests

**File: `apps/web/src/game/Zone.test.tsx`**

Header comment: `// B3.1 rule 6, R383, R64: what a held zone's icon says it is held for.`

Imports:
- `cleanup`, `render`, `screen` from `@testing-library/react`
- `afterEach`, `describe`, `expect`, `it` from `vitest`
- `CATALOG` from `@jackioh/cards`
- `type PlayerView`, `type Row` from `@jackioh/shared`
- `baseView`, `emptySide`, `unit` from `../test/fixtures.ts`
- `CatalogContext`, `lookupFromDefs` from `./catalog.ts`
- `testid`, `type Side` from `./contract.ts`
- `Zone` (the default export) from `./Zone.tsx`

Helpers:
- `const HELD_LANE_2 = { units: [false, false, false, false, false], backrow: [false, true, false, false, false] };`
- `function animated(owner: "p1" | "p2")` returns `unit(owner, { instanceId: \`spatula-${owner}\`, defId: "classicplus-012-8", attack: 10, maxHealth: 3, health: 3, keywords: [{ kind: "Rush" }], animated: { home: 2 } })`. That card is Frostspatula in the catalog.
- `function heldTitle(view: PlayerView, side: Side, row: Row, lane: number): string | null`:
  - renders `<CatalogContext.Provider value={lookup}><Zone view={view} side={side} row={row} lane={lane} /></CatalogContext.Provider>`;
  - returns `screen.getByTestId(testid.zone(side, row, lane)).querySelector(".reserved-icon")?.getAttribute("title") ?? null`.

`describe("B3.1 rule 6, R64: a held zone's icon says what it is held for", …)` holds these tests:

1. `it("R383 your held backrow zone names the animated card that goes back to it")`
   - View: `baseView({ you: emptySide("p1", { units: [animated("p1"), null, null, null, null], reserved: HELD_LANE_2 }) })`.
   - Assert `heldTitle(view, "you", "backrow", 2)` is `"Held for Frostspatula to return"`.

2. `it("R383 the opponent's held backrow zone names their animated card the same way")`
   - View: `baseView({ opponent: emptySide("p2", { hand: { count: 4 }, units: [animated("p2"), null, null, null, null], reserved: HELD_LANE_2 }) })`.
   - Assert `heldTitle(view, "opponent", "backrow", 2)` is `"Held for Frostspatula to return"`.

3. `it("R64 a held zone no animated card goes back to keeps the Reborn wording")`. Three renders, with `cleanup()` between them. Each expects `"Held for a Reborn unit"`:
   - (a) On the `you` side, `reserved: { units: [false, true, false, false, false], backrow: [false, false, false, false, false] }`, with `animated("p1")` in units lane 1. Check `heldTitle(view, "you", "units", 2)`: a unit zone is never a home.
   - (b) On the `you` side, `reserved: { units: [false,false,false,false,false], backrow: [false, false, true, false, false] }`, with `animated("p1")` (home 2). Check `heldTitle(view, "you", "backrow", 3)`: the home is a different lane.
   - (c) The `you` side has `reserved: HELD_LANE_2` and no units. The opponent has `animated("p2")` in units lane 1. Check `heldTitle(view, "you", "backrow", 2)`: a card on the other seat does not name this seat's zone.

Commands (if the `@jackioh/*` imports fail to resolve, run `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` first):

```
pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/game/Zone.test.tsx src/i18n/i18n.test.ts
pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/cards/cardState.test.tsx src/game/Board.test.tsx
pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck
pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/game/Zone.tsx apps/web/src/game/Zone.test.tsx
cargo jackioh spec check
```

The second line runs the existing tests that render `Zone` through `Board`, as a regression check. `spec check` is there because the new test and comments cite R64 and R383. Both notes exist, so it should stay green.

## Done when

- [ ] A held backrow zone whose lane is the `animated.home` of a unit on its own side has the icon title "Held for {name} to return", with the unit's face name (tests 1 and 2).
- [ ] Every other held zone keeps "Held for a Reborn unit" (test 3).
- [ ] `zh-CN.json` has the new entry, and `i18n.test.ts` passes, including its untranslated-sentence and token-match tests.
- [ ] `Zone.test.tsx`, `cardState.test.tsx` and `Board.test.tsx` pass.
- [ ] Typecheck and eslint are clean, and `cargo jackioh spec check` is green.
- [ ] Only the three files in the table are changed.

## Risks

- **Hidden information (CLAUDE.md rule 7):** the name comes only from a `UnitView` already on the field, through `listedFace`. `listedFace` returns null for the hidden sentinel, and the tooltip then falls back to the Reborn wording, so nothing hidden can show. Do not look at backrow entries, hands or piles.
- **Rules of hooks:** `useContext` must stay unconditional at the top of `Zone`, never inside the `reserved &&` branch.
- **i18n guard:** a `t()` call whose first argument is not a string literal escapes `i18n.test.ts`'s check. Keep both literals as written in step 2.
- **Rendering cost:** `heldFor` runs only for held zones, because it sits inside the `&&` branch.
- There is no engine, wire, replay or determinism impact, because nothing outside `apps/web` changes.

## Open questions

Decisions I made that the issue left open:
- **The name the tooltip uses.** It is `listedFace(...).name`, the name the card's face shows. That covers Chinese faces (R1301), Glitch and match-made definitions. I rejected `useCardInfo(defId).name`, because it misses the Chinese flag on a card.
- **A card whose control has changed.** If an animated card is stolen, its home stays held on its old side until cleanup (`crates/engine/src/animated.rs`, `return_home`). `animated.home` doesn't say which side the home is on, so the old side's held zone keeps the Reborn wording, as the issue proposes. I rejected matching units on the other seat, because the view can't tell that case apart from a home on that seat's own side. Test 3(c) pins this. If people want different wording there, it needs a side added to `AnimatedView` in the engine, which would be a separate issue.
- **The zone's `aria-label`.** It stays "Reserved zone". The issue changes only the `title`.
````
